population.span: in adults without diabetes (N = 611) and with either overweight (body mass index ≥27) plus at least 1 comorbidity or obesity (body mass index ≥30).

endpoint.span: The co–primary end points were percentage change in body weight and the loss of 5% or more of baseline weight by week 68.

estimate.span: At week 68, the estimated mean body weight change from baseline was –16.0% for semaglutide vs –5.7% for placebo (difference, −10.3 percentage points [95% CI, −12.0 to −8.6]; P < .001).

ci.span: At week 68, the estimated mean body weight change from baseline was –16.0% for semaglutide vs –5.7% for placebo (difference, −10.3 percentage points [95% CI, −12.0 to −8.6]; P < .001).

analysis_set.span: the treatment policy estimand (similar to an intention-to-treat analysis), which quantified the average treatment effect among all randomized participants, regardless of adherence to treatment or initiation of rescue interventions (ie, antiobesity medications or bariatric surgery).

treatment_strategy.span: Participants were randomized (2:1) to semaglutide, 2.4 mg (n = 407) or placebo (n = 204), both combined with a low-calorie diet for the first 8 weeks and intensive behavioral therapy (ie, 30 counseling visits) during 68 weeks.

follow_up.span: At week 68, the estimated mean body weight change from baseline was –16.0% for semaglutide vs –5.7% for placebo (difference, −10.3 percentage points [95% CI, −12.0 to −8.6]; P < .001).

served_mismatch: The served means −16.5 and −5.8 are registry available-data summaries for the in-trial observation period, with 373 and 189 participants contributing data, respectively. The served sample sizes 407 and 204 are total randomized denominators, not the denominators for those summaries. These summaries do not represent the requested treatment-policy estimate with missing-data handling. The full text reports a treatment-policy mean difference of −10.3 percentage points (95% CI −12.0 to −8.6), with estimated arm changes of −16.0% and −5.7%.
